cards.front: In the developing neural tube, what do the alar and basal plates become?
cards.back: The **sulcus limitans** separates them. **Alar plate** (dorsal): **sensory** neurons, such as the dorsal horn. **Basal plate** (ventral): **motor** neurons, such as the ventral horn. In the brainstem, motor nuclei lie **medial** and sensory nuclei lie **lateral**.
cards.back_pt: O **sulco limitante** separa as duas. **Placa alar** (dorsal): neurônios **sensitivos**, como o corno dorsal. **Placa basal** (ventral): neurônios **motores**, como o corno ventral. No tronco encefálico, os núcleos motores ficam **mediais** e os sensitivos ficam **laterais**.

cards.front: Which adult structures come from each secondary brain vesicle?
cards.back: **Telencephalon**: cerebral hemispheres, lateral ventricles. **Diencephalon**: thalamus, hypothalamus, third ventricle. **Mesencephalon**: midbrain, cerebral aqueduct. **Metencephalon**: pons, cerebellum. **Myelencephalon**: medulla. The last two surround the **fourth ventricle**.
cards.back_pt: **Telencéfalo**: hemisférios cerebrais, ventrículos laterais. **Diencéfalo**: tálamo, hipotálamo, terceiro ventrículo. **Mesencéfalo**: o próprio mesencéfalo, aqueduto cerebral. **Metencéfalo**: ponte, cerebelo. **Mielencéfalo**: bulbo. Os dois últimos envolvem o **quarto ventrículo**.

cards.front: What is holoprosencephaly, and what is its classic molecular cause?
cards.back: The **prosencephalon** fails to split into two hemispheres. Classic cause: loss of **sonic hedgehog (SHH)** signaling. Midline face defects follow: **hypotelorism**, **cyclopia**, cleft lip and palate. Linked to **trisomy 13 (Patau)** and fetal alcohol exposure.
cards.back_pt: O **prosencéfalo** não se divide em dois hemisférios. Causa clássica: perda da sinalização de **sonic hedgehog (SHH)**. Seguem-se defeitos faciais de linha média: **hipotelorismo**, **ciclopia**, fenda labial e palatina. Associada à **trissomia do 13 (Patau)** e à exposição fetal ao álcool.

cards.front: How do Chiari I and Chiari II malformations differ?
cards.back: **Chiari I**: only the cerebellar **tonsils** descend through the foramen magnum; often found in adolescents or adults with occipital headache; linked to **syringomyelia**. **Chiari II**: **vermis**, tonsils and medulla descend; seen in infants with **lumbosacral myelomeningocele** and **hydrocephalus**.
cards.back_pt: **Chiari I**: só as **tonsilas** cerebelares descem pelo forame magno; geralmente achada em adolescentes ou adultos com cefaleia occipital; associada à **siringomielia**. **Chiari II**: **verme**, tonsilas e bulbo descem; ocorre em lactentes com **mielomeningocele lombossacra** e **hidrocefalia**.

cards.front: Trace the path of CSF from production to absorption.
cards.back: **Choroid plexus** → lateral ventricles → **interventricular foramina (Monro)** → third ventricle → **cerebral aqueduct** → fourth ventricle → **foramina of Luschka** (lateral) and **Magendie** (median) → subarachnoid space → **arachnoid granulations** → dural venous sinuses.
cards.back_pt: **Plexo coroide** → ventrículos laterais → **forames interventriculares (Monro)** → terceiro ventrículo → **aqueduto cerebral** → quarto ventrículo → **forames de Luschka** (laterais) e **de Magendie** (mediano) → espaço subaracnóideo → **granulações aracnóideas** → seios venosos durais.

cards.front: Which cranial nerves leave the skull through the anterior and middle cranial fossae, and through which openings?
cards.back: **Cribriform plate**: CN I. **Optic canal**: CN II. **Superior orbital fissure**: CN III, IV, V1 and VI. **Foramen rotundum**: V2. **Foramen ovale**: V3.
cards.back_pt: **Lâmina cribriforme**: NC I. **Canal óptico**: NC II. **Fissura orbital superior**: NC III, IV, V1 e VI. **Forame redondo**: V2. **Forame oval**: V3.

cards.front: What does each main thalamic relay nucleus carry?
cards.back: **VPL**: pain, temperature, touch and position sense from the **body**. **VPM**: the same from the **face**, plus **taste**. **LGN**: **vision**. **MGN**: **hearing**. **VL**: motor loops from the basal ganglia and cerebellum.
cards.back_pt: **VPL**: dor, temperatura, tato e propriocepção do **corpo**. **VPM**: o mesmo da **face**, mais o **paladar**. **CGL** (corpo geniculado lateral): **visão**. **CGM** (corpo geniculado medial): **audição**. **VL**: circuitos motores dos núcleos da base e do cerebelo.

cards.front: How do the direct and indirect basal ganglia pathways change movement?
cards.back: **Direct**: striatum inhibits **GPi**, releasing the thalamus → **more movement**. **Indirect**: striatum inhibits **GPe**, which frees the **subthalamic nucleus** to excite GPi → **less movement**. Dopamine from the **SNc** excites direct (**D1**) and inhibits indirect (**D2**).
cards.back_pt: **Direta**: o estriado inibe o **GPi**, liberando o tálamo → **mais movimento**. **Indireta**: o estriado inibe o **GPe**, o que libera o **núcleo subtalâmico** para excitar o GPi → **menos movimento**. A dopamina da **SNc** excita a via direta (**D1**) e inibe a indireta (**D2**).

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 17 weeks of gestation comes for prenatal care. She has epilepsy treated with valproic acid and did not take any vitamins before or during the pregnancy. Maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein is elevated. Amniotic fluid shows high alpha-fetoprotein and high acetylcholinesterase. Ultrasound shows a sac over the lower lumbar spine that contains spinal cord and nerve roots. Which developmental failure best explains this finding?
choices: Failure of the prosencephalon to divide into two hemispheres
Failure of the vertebral arches to fuse over a normally closed neural tube
Failure of the caudal (posterior) neuropore to close
Failure of neural crest cells to migrate to the bowel wall
Failure of the cranial (anterior) neuropore to close
questions.explanation: A sac that holds spinal cord and nerve roots is a **myelomeningocele**, an open defect from failed closure of the **caudal neuropore** in week 4. Open defects leak fetal proteins, so **AFP** and amniotic **acetylcholinesterase** rise; valproate and low **folic acid** raise the risk. **Spina bifida occulta** (unfused vertebral arches only) is closed, so AFP stays normal and there is no sac. Failure of the cranial neuropore causes anencephaly.
questions.explanation_pt: Um saco que contém medula espinal e raízes nervosas é uma **mielomeningocele**, defeito aberto por falha no fechamento do **neuroporo caudal** na 4ª semana. Defeitos abertos deixam escapar proteínas fetais, então a **AFP** e a **acetilcolinesterase** do líquido amniótico sobem; o valproato e a falta de **ácido fólico** aumentam o risco. A **espinha bífida oculta** (apenas arcos vertebrais não fundidos) é fechada, então a AFP fica normal e não há saco. A falha do neuroporo cranial causa anencefalia.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old man has had 8 months of worsening walking. His wife says he takes short, shuffling steps and his feet seem stuck to the floor. He also has urinary urgency with incontinence and has become forgetful. There is no tremor or rigidity. CT of the head shows enlargement of all four ventricles, out of proportion to the cortical sulci. Lumbar puncture shows a normal opening pressure, and his gait improves for 2 days after removal of a large volume of CSF. Which mechanism best explains his condition?
choices: Reduced CSF absorption at the arachnoid granulations
Narrowing of the cerebral aqueduct
Overproduction of CSF by a choroid plexus tumor
Loss of brain tissue with passive ventricular enlargement
Obstruction of the outflow foramina of the fourth ventricle
questions.explanation: Gait disturbance, urinary incontinence and dementia with large ventricles point to **normal pressure hydrocephalus**, a **communicating** hydrocephalus from poor CSF reabsorption at the **arachnoid granulations**. The gait response to CSF removal supports the diagnosis. **Hydrocephalus ex vacuo** (brain atrophy) is the most tempting choice, but the sulci would enlarge as much as the ventricles, and removing CSF would not help. Aqueductal or fourth-ventricle obstruction would cause noncommunicating hydrocephalus with raised pressure.
questions.explanation_pt: Distúrbio da marcha, incontinência urinária e demência com ventrículos aumentados indicam **hidrocefalia de pressão normal**, uma hidrocefalia **comunicante** por reabsorção deficiente de LCR nas **granulações aracnóideas**. A melhora da marcha após a retirada de LCR apoia o diagnóstico. A **hidrocefalia ex vacuo** (atrofia cerebral) é a alternativa mais tentadora, mas os sulcos aumentariam tanto quanto os ventrículos, e retirar LCR não ajudaria. A obstrução do aqueduto ou do quarto ventrículo causaria hidrocefalia não comunicante com pressão elevada.

questions.stem: A 51-year-old woman has 4 months of hoarseness and trouble swallowing. Exam shows that the uvula deviates to the right when she says 'ah', and the gag reflex is absent on the left. Her left shoulder droops, and she is weak when she turns her head to the right against resistance. The tongue protrudes in the midline. Facial movement and hearing are normal. MRI shows an enhancing mass at the left skull base. Through which opening do all the affected nerves pass?
choices: Hypoglossal canal
Internal acoustic meatus
Foramen ovale
Jugular foramen
Foramen magnum
questions.explanation: The deficits involve **CN IX** (afferent limb of the gag reflex), **CN X** (efferent limb of the gag, hoarseness, dysphagia, uvula pulled away from the lesion) and **CN XI** (left sternocleidomastoid and trapezius weakness). All three leave the skull through the **jugular foramen**, together with the internal jugular vein. The **hypoglossal canal** is tempting because it is close by, but CN XII damage would push the tongue toward the lesion, and here the tongue is midline. Normal face and hearing exclude the internal acoustic meatus.
questions.explanation_pt: Os déficits envolvem o **NC IX** (via aferente do reflexo nauseoso), o **NC X** (via eferente do reflexo nauseoso, rouquidão, disfagia, úvula desviada para longe da lesão) e o **NC XI** (fraqueza do esternocleidomastóideo e do trapézio à esquerda). Os três saem do crânio pelo **forame jugular**, junto com a veia jugular interna. O **canal do hipoglosso** é tentador por ser vizinho, mas a lesão do NC XII desviaria a língua para o lado da lesão, e aqui a língua está na linha média. Face e audição normais excluem o meato acústico interno.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old woman with a history of lung cancer has 3 weeks of clumsiness in her right hand. She spills drinks and misses buttons. On finger-to-nose testing, her right hand shakes more as it nears the target and overshoots it. Rapid alternating movements are slow and irregular on the right. When she walks, she drifts to the right. Strength, reflexes and sensation are normal in all limbs. Where is the lesion most likely located?
choices: Left cerebellar hemisphere
Right cerebellar hemisphere
Cerebellar vermis
Left internal capsule
Right dorsal column of the spinal cord
questions.explanation: Intention tremor, **dysmetria** and **dysdiadochokinesia** in one arm point to the **cerebellar hemisphere** on the **same side**. Cerebellar output crosses once to the opposite motor cortex, and the corticospinal tract crosses back, so the deficit is ipsilateral. The left hemisphere is the most tempting choice, but it would affect the left limbs. A **vermis** lesion causes mainly truncal ataxia and a wide-based gait, with less limb involvement.
questions.explanation_pt: Tremor de intenção, **dismetria** e **disdiadococinesia** em um braço indicam lesão do **hemisfério cerebelar** do **mesmo lado**. A eferência cerebelar cruza uma vez para o córtex motor oposto, e o trato corticoespinal cruza de volta, então o déficit é ipsilateral. O hemisfério esquerdo é a alternativa mais tentadora, mas afetaria os membros esquerdos. Uma lesão do **verme** causa principalmente ataxia de tronco e marcha de base alargada, com menor envolvimento dos membros.

notes.title: Neuroanatomy and neuroembryology: the essentials
notes.body_md:
## Neural tube

- The neural tube closes in **week 4**. **Folic acid** before conception lowers the risk of defects.
- **Anencephaly**: cranial neuropore stays open; high AFP, polyhydramnios.
- **Spina bifida occulta**: unfused vertebral arches, intact skin (often a tuft of hair), normal AFP.
- **Meningocele**: meninges herniate. **Myelomeningocele**: meninges plus spinal cord; high AFP and amniotic acetylcholinesterase.
- **Neural crest** gives rise to peripheral ganglia, Schwann cells, melanocytes and the adrenal medulla.
- **Dandy-Walker**: small or absent vermis with a cystic, enlarged fourth ventricle.

## Ventricles and CSF

- **Noncommunicating** hydrocephalus: a block inside the ventricles (for example, aqueductal stenosis).
- **Communicating** hydrocephalus: poor absorption at the arachnoid granulations.
- **Normal pressure hydrocephalus**: gait problems, urinary incontinence and dementia.

## Meninges

- Dura, arachnoid, pia from outside in. **Epidural space**: between skull and dura (middle meningeal artery).
- **Subdural space**: crossed by **bridging veins**. **Subarachnoid space**: CSF and the major arteries.

## Brainstem and cranial nerves

- Midbrain: CN III, IV (IV exits dorsally). Pons: V-VIII (VI-VIII exit at the pontomedullary junction). Medulla: IX, X, XII.
- **Internal acoustic meatus**: VII, VIII. **Jugular foramen**: IX, X, XI. **Hypoglossal canal**: XII.

## Blood supply

- **Circle of Willis**: anterior cerebral and anterior communicating arteries, internal carotids, posterior communicating and posterior cerebral arteries.
- **ACA**: medial surface (leg area). **MCA**: lateral surface (face, arm, language). **PCA**: occipital lobe.
- Two vertebral arteries join to form the **basilar artery**.

## Cerebellum and limbic system

- **Vermis**: trunk and gait. **Hemispheres**: limbs on the **same side**.
- **Hippocampus**: new memory. **Amygdala**: fear. **Mammillary bodies**: memory circuit; damaged in thiamine deficiency.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Tubo neural

- O tubo neural fecha na **4ª semana**. **Ácido fólico** antes da concepção reduz o risco de defeitos.
- **Anencefalia**: o neuroporo cranial fica aberto; AFP alta, polidrâmnio.
- **Espinha bífida oculta**: arcos vertebrais não fundidos, pele íntegra (muitas vezes um tufo de pelos), AFP normal.
- **Meningocele**: herniação das meninges. **Mielomeningocele**: meninges mais medula espinal; AFP e acetilcolinesterase amniótica altas.
- A **crista neural** origina gânglios periféricos, células de Schwann, melanócitos e a medula adrenal.
- **Dandy-Walker**: verme pequeno ou ausente com quarto ventrículo cístico e aumentado.

## Ventrículos e LCR

- Hidrocefalia **não comunicante**: bloqueio dentro dos ventrículos (por exemplo, estenose do aqueduto).
- Hidrocefalia **comunicante**: absorção deficiente nas granulações aracnóideas.
- **Hidrocefalia de pressão normal**: distúrbio da marcha, incontinência urinária e demência.

## Meninges

- Dura-máter, aracnoide e pia-máter, de fora para dentro. **Espaço epidural**: entre o crânio e a dura (artéria meníngea média).
- **Espaço subdural**: atravessado pelas **veias em ponte**. **Espaço subaracnóideo**: LCR e as grandes artérias.

## Tronco encefálico e nervos cranianos

- Mesencéfalo: NC III, IV (o IV sai pela face dorsal). Ponte: V-VIII (VI-VIII emergem no sulco bulbopontino). Bulbo: IX, X, XII.
- **Meato acústico interno**: VII, VIII. **Forame jugular**: IX, X, XI. **Canal do hipoglosso**: XII.

## Irrigação

- **Polígono de Willis**: artérias cerebrais anteriores e comunicante anterior, carótidas internas, comunicantes posteriores e cerebrais posteriores.
- **ACA**: face medial (área da perna). **ACM**: face lateral (face, braço, linguagem). **ACP**: lobo occipital.
- As duas artérias vertebrais se unem e formam a **artéria basilar**.

## Cerebelo e sistema límbico

- **Verme**: tronco e marcha. **Hemisférios**: membros do **mesmo lado**.
- **Hipocampo**: memória nova. **Amígdala**: medo. **Corpos mamilares**: circuito da memória; lesados na deficiência de tiamina.
